findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether pytest locates an ini/config file from the repo cwd for these children. Either also pass `--confcutdir <same dir>` (skipped when the caller passed one), or show that `--rootdir` alone moves confcutdir in that configuration.
evidence: Root cause step 1: "with no ini file, rootdir = get_common_ancestor(...)"
Root cause step 2 names `_is_in_confcutdir` as the gate for the ancestor walk.
pytest Config: `confcutdir = inipath.parent if inipath is not None else rootpath`. `--rootdir` overrides rootpath only.
The child's cwd is the repo, which normally carries pytest configuration.
findings.finding: The fix may not change confcutdir in the actual failing configuration. pytest sets confcutdir to `inipath.parent` whenever an ini or config file is located, and only falls back to rootpath when none is found. `--rootdir` does not stop the ini search. On cross-drive Windows the search ancestor stays the cwd (the repo). If the repo has a pyproject.toml, pytest.ini, tox.ini or setup.cfg that pytest picks up, confcutdir stays `D:\a\rebar\rebar` after the fix. Collection would then still start at `C:\` and scan `%TEMP%`. The plan asserts "with no ini file" but never establishes that no ini is located from the repo cwd for these children. The collection walk is governed by `_is_in_confcutdir`, so confcutdir is the knob that actually matters.
findings.location: Approach — "the helper adds `--rootdir <common directory of those arguments>`. This pins the outcome POSIX already gets: rootdir and confcutdir become the test file's own directory"
scenarios: Windows sweep: the repo cwd contains a pyproject.toml that pytest locates as its config file. The fix adds `--rootdir C:\...\test_dir`, but confcutdir stays the repo. The `rebar-ticket-view-*` lstat race still fires.
findings.suggested_fix: Append both `--rootdir <dir>` and `--confcutdir <dir>`, keeping the same caller-override guard. Confcutdir is what bounds the ancestor walk in `Session.collect`, regardless of whether an inipath is found.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define which argv items count as path arguments (for example, items not starting with `-` and not the value of a known value-taking option), and match the opt-out flags in both `--flag value` and `--flag=value`/`-cVALUE` forms. evidence: Approach: "When the caller's absolute path arguments (the part before any `::`) all lie outside the child's cwd, and the caller passed none of `--rootdir`, `-c`, `--config-file` or `--confcutdir`"
Testing lists only relative, under-cwd, caller-flag and cross-drive cases; it has no option-value case.
findings.finding: The plan does not say how 'path arguments' are separated from absolute option values, or how the opt-out flags are matched in their joined forms. Option values such as `--basetemp <abs>`, `--junitxml=<abs>` or `-p <mod>`, if counted as path arguments, would widen the computed common directory. Joined spellings such as `--rootdir=X`, `--confcutdir=X` or `-cX` could slip past the 'caller passed none of' check.
findings.location: Approach ("the caller's absolute path arguments" / "caller passed none of `--rootdir`, `-c`, `--config-file` or `--confcutdir`")
scenarios: A caller passes `--basetemp C:\...\bt` plus a test file: the common directory moves up toward %TEMP%, collection lists shared temp again, and the race returns.
A caller passes `--rootdir=D:\x`: the helper appends a second --rootdir, and the later one silently wins.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how option values are excluded from "path arguments" (e.g. only arguments not starting with `-` and not consumed as an option's value), and add pure-function tests with an absolute-valued option such as `--basetemp`/`--junitxml`.
evidence: No rule is given for separating positional arguments from option values.
No test case covers an option whose value is an absolute path.
findings.finding: The plan does not say how the function distinguishes positional path arguments from option values. Absolute values passed to options such as `--basetemp C:\...`, `--junitxml C:\...\out.xml`, `-p`, `-o`, `--rootdir`-like plugin options, or `-k`/`-m` expressions would be read as "absolute path arguments outside the cwd". That yields a wrong `--rootdir`, or suppresses it when mixed with in-cwd paths.
findings.location: Approach — "When the caller's absolute path arguments (the part before any `::`) all lie outside the child's cwd"
scenarios: A caller passes `--basetemp C:\Temp\bt` plus a repo-relative test. The function treats `C:\Temp\bt` as a path argument, and the outcome depends on the unspecified "all" versus "any" handling.
A caller passes `--junitxml <tmp>/r.xml` plus a test under tmp. The common directory is computed over the xml path too.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the guard and its tests cover `--opt=value` and `-cVALUE` forms for every guarded option.

findings.finding: The caller-override guard does not specify the alternate option spellings it must recognise: `--rootdir=X`, `--confcutdir=X`, `--config-file=X`, and the attached short form `-cX`. If only space-separated forms are matched, the helper appends a second `--rootdir` that silently overrides the caller's choice (last one wins).
findings.location: Approach — "the caller passed none of `--rootdir`, `-c`, `--config-file` or `--confcutdir`"; Testing — "A caller-supplied `--rootdir`/`-c`/`--confcutdir` gives nothing"
scenarios: A caller passes `--rootdir=/some/dir`, the guard misses it, and the helper's appended `--rootdir` replaces the caller's.
findings.suggested_fix: Match each argument by prefix: `a == opt or a.startswith(opt + '=')` for the long options, and `a.startswith('-c')` excluding other `-c`-prefixed long options, with a test per spelling.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Say exactly which argv entries are path arguments: positional only, never values of options. Add `--rootdir` only when every positional path argument is absolute and outside cwd, so any relative positional disables it. Add pure-function tests for the mixed relative+absolute case and an absolute option-value case.
evidence: Plan: "When the caller's absolute path arguments (the part before any `::`) all lie outside the child's cwd ... the helper adds `--rootdir <common directory of those arguments>`"
Plan: "Path arguments inside the cwd (repo-relative test files) get no new option, so their rootdir, ini file and conftest loading are unchanged."

Callers already mix options that take a separate value with positional args, e.g. test_engine_dir.py:184-196 (`-k <expr>`, `-p no:randomly`) and test_ci_workflow_parity.py:679-693 (`-m selection`, *paths). The rule has no way to tell option values from positional args.
findings.finding: The trigger rule doesn't say which argv entries are 'path arguments'. As written ('the caller's absolute path arguments ... all lie outside the child's cwd') it will misfire in two ways. (a) An absolute value given to an option as a separate argument (e.g. `--junitxml <tmp>/x.xml`, `--ignore <abs>`, `--deselect <abs>::t`) counts as a path argument. (b) Relative path arguments are ignored. So a run with only repo-relative test paths plus one absolute option value, or one with repo-relative paths plus an absolute tmp file, gets `--rootdir <tmp dir>`. That contradicts the plan's promise that 'Path arguments inside the cwd ... get no new option, so their rootdir, ini file and conftest loading are unchanged'.
findings.location: Approach — the --rootdir trigger condition in tests/_nested_pytest.py
scenarios: A caller passes `tests/unit/x.py` (relative) plus an absolute tmp_path probe. The rule sees one absolute arg outside cwd and pins rootdir to the probe's directory, which changes rootdir and node ids for the repo test.
A future caller passes `--junitxml <tmp>/report.xml` with repo-relative tests. The report path is taken as a path argument and rootdir moves to tmp.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `--rootdir` only when every positional argument (an entry that does not start with `-` and is not the value of a preceding option that takes a separate value) is absolute and lies outside cwd. If any positional is relative, or there are no positionals, add nothing. Add pure-function tests for `['tests/x.py', '<C:abs>']` → nothing and `['--junitxml', '<C:abs>.xml', 'tests/x.py']` → nothing.

The plan also never says whether the path-argument scan skips option values such as `-p name`, `-k expr` or `-m expr`, which could be mistaken for path arguments.

First, `run_nested_pytest` accepts `cwd=None` (inherit the parent's cwd; test_nested_pytest_helper.py:93 uses it), and the plan doesn't say which cwd the decision compares against in that case. Applying `dirname` to every argument instead turns a directory argument into its parent, so an absolute directory directly under %TEMP% (e.g. from `tempfile.mkdtemp`) would pin rootdir/confcutdir to %TEMP%. Session.collect would then scan %TEMP% again, which is exactly the race being fixed.

findings.finding: pytest raises a UsageError when `--rootdir` does not name an existing directory. The plan says the decision function uses 'string functions only' and adds '--rootdir <common directory of those arguments>'. A string-only function cannot tell a file argument from a directory argument, and `pathmod.commonpath([single_file])` returns the file path itself. pytest's own get_common_ancestor checks the filesystem with `is_file()` to take the parent. As specified, the helper will either pass a file path to `--rootdir` (child exits with a usage error) or always take dirname, which widens rootdir to the parent of a directory argument.

findings.suggested_fix: Give the pure function an injectable `is_file` predicate (default `os.path.isfile`) next to `pathmod`. For each argument, strip `::...`, map files to `pathmod.dirname`, then take `pathmod.commonpath` of the results inside the ValueError guard. In the ntpath tests, pass a stub predicate.
